statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 3 and far below the block threshold because CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z, leaving no Nasdaq-100 price path to score; the last observed path, Friday's record 31,017.53 intraday high fully retraced into a 30,807.93 close in the lower quarter of the 30,737.07-31,017.53 range with VIX down 6.59% to 15.31, was orderly two-way discovery rather than the extension pattern Tail measures. Stress holds at 75 in the high band: the Riyadh refinery fire remains unconfirmed by Saudi authorities and Aramco and Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa were reported early Sunday, but Friday's oil tape fell to an $88.06 intraday low and the G7 has committed up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves, which is a real supply-side counterweight rather than an escalation-only picture. Confidence is 85 on independently re-verified session levels, yields, oil and a full week-ahead calendar against an unresolved damage question and no live price path.
recommendation: Tail stays in the low band for the first nineteen scored hours, so the deterministic mapping remains EA_ON and green through 21:00Z while the weekend halt runs. The three hours from the 22:00Z CME restart carry Tail 22, 23 and 21, which maps to WATCH and yellow: that is the mildest cautionary band and reflects roughly 49 hours of accumulated news repricing into the thinnest books of the week, with a claimed strike on Saudi refining capacity, the G7 reserve release and the OPEC+ November decision all landing in the same print. Tail returns to the low band at 18 by 01:00Z on 5 October. The Saudi cash session from roughly 07:00Z to 12:00Z is the only live venue with direct exposure to the strike; under the inherited delayed-evidence rule it can inform Stress and Confidence but cannot establish current Nasdaq-100 structure or the current mapped state. A narrow danger window is published across the three restart hours. The next scheduled U.S. macro checkpoint is ISM Services at 14:00Z on 5 October, with FOMC minutes on 7 October.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 3 with no Nasdaq-100 price path to score, while a still-unconfirmed Riyadh refinery strike meeting a verified G7 100-million-barrel reserve release holds Stress at 75 and keeps the three hours after the 22:00Z restart in the watch band
body:
Friday 2 October remains the last traded session and its levels were independently re-verified for this publication. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, inside a 30,737.07-31,017.53 session range whose high is also the 52-week high. The detail that matters most for this framework is unchanged: the new intraday record at 31,017.53 was fully retraced and the index finished in the lower quarter of its own daily range. That is orderly two-way price discovery, not the shallow-pullback extension or failed-retracement pattern that defines Tail, so Tail holds at 3. VIX closed at 15.31, down 6.59% from 16.39 inside a 15.30-16.24 range, confirming volatility decay into the halt.

The session's driver was the September employment report: nonfarm payrolls rose 29,000 against a 90,000 consensus, the unemployment rate was 4.2% against 4.1% expected, monthly wage growth slowed to 0.1% against 0.3% expected and the prior two months were revised down by a combined 60,000. Equities read that as putting an October Fed hike on the back foot, with money markets pricing under a 25% chance of an increase, but the curve did not follow. The 2-year finished at 4.8414%, up 5.44 basis points, and the 10-year at 5.2939%, up 5.99 basis points, so a soft labour print was met with a higher long end. The Federal Reserve H.15 release has been re-checked and still publishes only through 1 October, where the 2-year stands at 4.78% and the 10-year at 5.24%, so Friday's reversal is carried from market reporting rather than from the official series.

The weekend's open question is the fire observed on Saturday 3 October near Aramco's refinery south of Riyadh. The Houthis claimed an attack with ballistic missiles and drones. Physical corroboration is on record from a Reuters witness, satellite imagery of storage tanks under heat and NASA FIRMS thermal detections, but as of this assessment neither Saudi authorities nor Aramco have confirmed an attack, damage, casualties or any refining, production or export impact, and reporting updated at 01:20Z on 4 October still records that absence. Escalation is running both ways: Houthi-run Al Masirah reported Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa early Sunday. Precedent from this conflict argues against treating the headline as an index-level path event on its own, since the March strike on Ras Tanura took that facility offline for about a week before it reopened and the August Jizan refinery fire was reported extinguished without capacity loss.

Two verified supply-side developments cut the other way and are the reason Stress is held rather than raised. On 2 October the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude and diesel reserves over four months, coordinated through the International Energy Agency and with a frontloaded diesel component inside the first 20 days, in response to Strait of Hormuz shipping constriction; U.S. diesel averaged $6.37 a gallon on the announcement date after a $6.52 record on 22 September. Oil itself fell on Friday: WTI settled near $91, down about 1.9%, after reaching an $88.06 one-month intraday low, while Brent at $102.25 was essentially unchanged. Separately, the eight OPEC+ countries in the monthly adjustment group hold a video conference today to review November output targets, with a rollover widely expected but not confirmed and the exact timing not independently verified. Absolute oil levels still carry a substantial war premium, which is what keeps Stress in the high band at 75, but a market pricing an imminent supply break does not print a one-month low two days earlier.

No live Nasdaq-100 evidence exists in this hour. CME equity-index futures have been halted since Friday 21:00Z and restart at 22:00Z on Sunday, so nineteen of the 24 forecast hours fall inside a window in which no price path can form at all. The shared Finviz context file was read as required and rejected for current use: its generatedAt is 29 September 2026 at 23:14Z, far beyond the 90-minute freshness limit, and its collectionStatus is partial with the calendar and futures sections unavailable. Stale supporting context was therefore not allowed to stand in for live structure, and the assessment rests on independent research. The restart hour is the genuine discontinuity: roughly 49 hours of accumulated news, an unquantified refining strike, the G7 release and the OPEC+ decision would all reprice into the thinnest books of the week, where a gap can extend without the retracements this framework depends on. That mechanism, not the importance of the news, is why the three restart hours sit in the watch band while everything else stays in the low band.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments and no slot required an unavailable entry. The window opens at 03:00Z on 3 October with Tail 8 and Stress 65 under a normal mode and decays as the halt takes hold: Tail falls from 8 to 3 by 12:00Z and stays at 3 for the remaining fifteen hours. Stress troughs at 52 around 14:00Z and then climbs steadily to 75 by 02:00Z on 4 October as the energy and Gulf escalation threads reopened and produced the fire at the Riyadh refinery. Confidence held in a narrow 82 to 88 range throughout, consistent with verified session levels and no live price path. Every slot carried the normal mode and no historical opinion was revised.
outlookSummary: Nineteen of the 24 forecast hours fall inside the CME equity-index weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them. Tail is held at 3 through 16:00Z, then lifts only gradually to 8 by 21:00Z on the restart approach, mapping to EA_ON and green for all nineteen halted hours. The three hours from 22:00Z carry Tail 22, 23 and 21, crossing into the watch band and mapping to WATCH and yellow on a dated discontinuity, the thinnest books of the week and a three-way catalyst stack of an unquantified refining strike, the G7 reserve release and the OPEC+ November decision. Tail then returns to the low band at 18 by 01:00Z and eases to 15 by 02:00Z. Stress runs from 75 to a peak of 79 into the restart and stays inside the high band throughout, easing back to 75 once a venue has priced the weekend's news for several hours. Confidence decays from 85 to a low of 77 before the restart as Friday's levels age, lifts during the Saudi cash session and recovers to 86 once live prices return. The dominant mode stays normal through the halt and shifts to mixed from 21:00Z on genuinely two-sided reopening scenarios.
